questions.question: What invariant makes an image vector directly comparable with a text vector in CLIP?
options: Both encoders must use the same Transformer weights.
Both outputs are projected to the same dimension and L2-normalized before similarity.
Every text must contain the image filename.
Both modalities must have the same number of input tokens.
questions.explanation: The towers can have different architectures and widths. Paired projections plus normalization create the common geometry used by the dot product.

questions.question: What is the lesson's core invariant about a text prompt?
options: It specifies the exact value of every output pixel.
It is a conditioning signal, so the candidate still needs evaluation against the intended result and release policy.
It selects an existing image from a search index.
It guarantees the same image on every runtime.
questions.explanation: A prompt steers a stochastic generator. It does not provide a complete pixel-level contract or eliminate output evaluation.

questions.question: What does the scheduler own in a diffusion inference loop?
options: It applies the model prediction to compute the next sample at the selected noise level.
It trains the text encoder from user prompts.
It decides whether the final image is legally safe to publish.
It stores the generated image in object storage.
questions.explanation: The denoiser predicts an update; the scheduler or sampler turns that prediction and current noise level into the next latent state.

questions.question: When is a text-to-image generation complete according to the lesson's core invariant?
options: As soon as the GPU decodes any pixels
After the prompt has been tokenized
After job state, policy decision, model configuration, output identity, and durable delivery are recorded
When the client has waited for the average model latency
questions.explanation: Candidate pixels remain untrusted. Completion requires a durable terminal state, governed release evidence, and an identified output.

questions.question: What is the lesson's core invariant for video generation?
options: Every frame must be identical.
A subject should change only when the intended action, camera plan, or shot boundary calls for it, not because state drifted accidentally.
The video must use the highest available frame rate.
A text prompt must determine every pixel and motion vector.
questions.explanation: Controlled continuity distinguishes intended change from accidental drift across frames, windows, and shots.
